answer: Age-scaled action cooldowns resist sybils: the minimum wait between an identity's consequential actions starts long at mint and shrinks only with proven continuous tenure, a beacon that brightens the longer it burns. A day-one fake acts only rarely; to push throughput an attacker must age each key down, a garden that ripens one season at a time. A farm's aggregate action-rate is bounded by sum of 1/cooldown, near zero for fresh keys, so burst-minting a river of identities yields almost no usable actions until each is aged. Honest agents act freely; mass-minted keys stay throttled.
